care_tips: Hand disinfection is one of the most important measures for infection prevention.
Always follow the 5-R principle for medication administration: Right patient, right medication, right dose, right time, right route.
Regular mobilization prevents thrombosis and pneumonia.
Good communication with patients and families is an important part of care.
Fluid intake and output should be regularly monitored in at-risk patients.
Fall prevention begins at admission - recognize and document risk factors.
Pressure ulcers are preventable - regular repositioning and skin inspection are essential.
Always ask about pain and adjust pain management individually.
Emergency medications should always be readily available and regularly checked for expiration dates.
Documentation should be timely and factual - it's also legally important.

wound_assessment.title: Wound Assessment
wound_assessment.subtitle: Systematic assessment of wounds with traffic light system
wound_assessment.intro: Please evaluate the wound according to the following criteria. This information helps document the healing process and optimize care.
tips: Always document wound changes promptly and with photos if possible.
Watch for signs of infection: redness, overheating, swelling, pain, exudate, odor.
The amount of exudate can provide clues about healing disorders or infections.
A clean, red wound base indicates good granulation.
Necrosis and debris should be documented and removed if necessary (as medically ordered).
wound_assessment.notes: All information serves standardized wound documentation and does not replace medical diagnosis.
wound_assessment.example: Example: Venous leg ulcer, medial lower leg, size 3x2cm, good granulation, little exudate, no odor, no signs of infection.

reddened.label: Reddened
reddened.description: Redness as a sign of inflammation

atemnot.title: Dyspnea
steps: Stay calm, reassure patient.
Elevate upper body.
Observe breathing (frequency, depth, sounds, cyanosis?).
Measure oxygen saturation (pulse oximeter). Target SpO2 >94%.
Oxygen administration according to medical order/standard.
Inform doctor.
Monitor vital signs (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2, temp, consciousness).
Documentation.

brustschmerz.title: Chest Pain
steps: Reassure patient, absolute rest.
Elevate upper body (with stable circulation!).
Check vital signs (BP, pulse (normal ~60-100/min), SpO2 (>94%)).
Pain assessment (scale 0-10, location, type, radiation).
Inform doctor IMMEDIATELY (suspected MI/ACS).
Perform 12-lead ECG.
Oxygen administration as ordered.
Prepare emergency medications (nitrospray etc.) as ordered.

hypoglykaemie.title: Hypoglycemia
steps: Recognize signs: cold sweats, trembling, hunger, pallor, palpitations, confusion, behavioral changes, visual disturbances.
Measure blood sugar immediately. Hypoglycemia often <60-70 mg/dl. (Normal range ~70-140 mg/dl).
If conscious & able to swallow: give fast-acting carbs (e.g. 2-4 glucose tablets, fruit juice/cola).
After 10-15 min: blood sugar check. If still low/persistent symptoms: repeat fast carbs & inform doctor!
With blood sugar stabilization: give slow-acting carbs (e.g. bread, yogurt, banana).
If unconscious/seizure: call emergency doctor (112)! Recovery position. NO oral food/fluid (aspiration risk!).
Glucagon injection i.m. as ordered (if unconscious/unable to swallow, if kit available/trained).
Monitor vital signs (pulse, BP, SpO2, consciousness). Document course & measures. Clarify cause.

sturz.title: Fall
steps: Address patient, reassure.
Check for obvious injuries (wounds, swelling, deformities).
Ask about pain (head, neck, spine, hip, limbs?).
Simple neurological check (pupils, orientation, motor function).
If suspected serious injury (e.g. fracture, head/spinal injury): Do not move! Call emergency doctor (112)!
For minor/no injuries: offer assistance with safe standing up.
Check vital signs (pulse, BP, SpO2, consciousness), possibly blood sugar.
Documentation (fall protocol), clarify cause.

fieber_sepsis.title: Fever
steps: Measure temperature (preferably rectal). Normal ~36.5-37.4°C.
Signs of sepsis? (qSOFA: RR ≥22/min, syst. BP ≤100mmHg, altered consciousness?). Chills?
If sepsis suspected: inform doctor IMMEDIATELY!
Increase fluid intake (oral/i.v. as ordered).
Calf compresses / fever-reducing measures as ordered.
Take blood cultures (before antibiotics, as ordered).
Monitor vital signs closely (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2, temp, consciousness, blood sugar).
Documentation.

blutung.title: Bleeding
steps: Stay calm, reassure patient.
Put on disposable gloves (self-protection!).
Apply direct pressure to wound (sterile compress/cloth).
Elevate affected extremity.
Apply pressure bandage.
Inform doctor / emergency doctor (112 for severe, uncontrollable bleeding).
Check vital signs (pulse, BP, SpO2, consciousness). Signs of shock? (tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, cold sweats)
For nosebleed: bend head forward, cool neck.

allergie_anaphylaxie.title: Allergy
steps: Stop allergen exposure (infusion, food, etc.).
Reassure patient. Positioning: dyspnea -> upper body elevated; shock -> lie flat, legs elevated.
Call emergency doctor (112), report anaphylaxis!
Check vital signs (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2, consciousness, skin).
Use epinephrine auto-injector (if available/trained).
Oxygen administration as ordered.
Be ready for resuscitation.
Documentation, secure trigger (if known).

krampfanfall.title: Seizure
steps: Stay calm, secure environment (remove objects).
Protect patient from injury (cushion head), do not restrain.
Do not put anything in mouth!
Observe seizure duration (note time!).
After seizure: recovery position (if unconscious).
Check breathing and SpO2.
Inform doctor. For first seizure, >5 min duration, injury or series -> emergency doctor (112)!
Documentation (type, duration, circumstances).

schlaganfallverdacht.title: Stroke
steps: FAST test: Face (smile), Arms (raise arms), Speech (repeat sentence), Time (time of symptom onset!).
If positive test: IMMEDIATELY call emergency doctor (112), report stroke!
Reassure patient, do not leave alone.
Position upper body slightly elevated (approx. 30 degrees).
Give nothing to eat or drink (aspiration risk!).
Check vital signs (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2, temp), check blood sugar!
Ask for/document exact time of symptom onset.
Prepare transport (documents, medications).

dehydratation.title: Dehydration
steps: Recognize signs: dry mucous membranes, skin tenting, confusion, oliguria (<0.5ml/kg/h), tachycardia, hypotension.
Offer/increase fluid intake (favorite drinks).
Keep fluid balance / monitor intake and output.
Clarify cause (intake, vomiting, diarrhea, fever?).
For severe dehydration / refusal: inform doctor (i.v. necessary?).
Check vital signs (pulse, BP, temp, skin turgor).
Perform/intensify oral care.
Documentation (intake, balance, symptoms, measures).

erbrechen_diarrhoe.title: Vomiting & Diarrhea
steps: Support patient (kidney dish, toilet).
Observe hygiene (gloves, gown), possibly isolation according to standard.
Compensate fluid/electrolyte loss (oral rehydration solution, i.v. as ordered).
Skin care in anal area (for diarrhea).
Observe excretions (frequency, amount, consistency, blood?).
For persistent, bloody, fever, severe discomfort: inform doctor.
Check vital signs (pulse, BP, temp). Signs of dehydration? (skin turgor, mucous membranes)
Documentation (frequency, consistency, balance, measures).

schmerz_akut.title: Acute Pain
steps: Take patient seriously. Pain assessment (scale 0-10, location, type, trigger).
Look for cause (new illness, complication?).
Adjust positioning, allow rest.
Non-pharmacological measures (cooling/warmth, relaxation, distraction).
Inform doctor. Give painkillers as ordered.
Check effectiveness of painkillers (reassessment after ~30-60 min).
Check vital signs (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2, consciousness - especially with opioids!).
Documentation (assessment, measures, effect).

verwirrtheit_delir.title: Confusion
steps: Radiate calm, reduce stimuli.
Provide orientation aids (name, date, place, glasses/hearing aid).
Check possible causes (infection, dehydration, pain, medications, hypoxia, urinary retention, etc.).
Inform doctor, have causes clarified!
Ensure safety (fall prevention), possibly constant observation.
Ensure fluid intake, nutrition.
Promote day-night rhythm.
Documentation (behavior, causes, measures).

schluckstoerung.title: Swallowing Disorder
steps: Recognize signs: coughing/clearing throat during/after eating, gurgling voice, food remains in mouth.
In acute aspiration (dyspnea, cyanosis): Emergency! Bend forward, encourage coughing, possibly Heimlich maneuver, emergency doctor (112)!
If suspected: stop food/fluid intake immediately!
Inform doctor, request speech therapy consultation.
Adapt diet consistency (thickening, etc.) as ordered/standard.
Keep upper body upright during & after eating (min. 30 min).
Oral care after meals.
Observe breathing/vital signs (RR, SpO2, temp - aspiration pneumonia?).

harnverhalt.title: Urinary Retention
steps: Ask patient about urination problems (urge? pain?).
Palpate lower abdomen (full bladder?).
Perform bladder scan.
Last urination? Monitor intake and output.
Supportive measures (run water, privacy).
Inform doctor (single catheterization/permanent catheter as ordered?).
Anuria (<100ml/24h) or <6h no urination despite urge/fluid intake? URGENT: inform doctor! (kidney failure?).
Documentation (symptoms, balance, measures, residual urine).

hypertensive_krise.title: Hypertensive Crisis
steps: Measure blood pressure (both arms). Normal ~120/80 mmHg.
Reassure patient, elevate upper body.
Ask about symptoms (headache, dizziness, visual disturbance, chest pain, dyspnea, nausea?).
Inform doctor IMMEDIATELY for BP >180/110 (crisis) or BP >230/120 / with symptoms (emergency)!
Give antihypertensives as ordered.
Monitor BP closely (goal: slow reduction!).
Clarify cause (medication compliance?).
Documentation (BP values, symptoms, medication).

wundinfektion.title: Wound Infection
steps: Inspect wound: redness, swelling, warmth, pain, exudate (amount, color, odor?), wound edge.
Dressing change according to hygiene principles.
Wound swab as ordered (before antiseptics!).
Inform doctor about wound condition.
Watch for systemic infection signs (fever, chills, tachycardia, lab values?).
Wound irrigation / antiseptics / dressings as ordered.
Pain management.
Documentation (wound condition, measures, materials).

synkope_kollaps.title: Unconsciousness
steps: Address patient, check consciousness.
If unconscious: check breathing! -> recovery position or resuscitation!
For brief unconsciousness / presyncope: lie down, legs elevated.
Check vital signs (pulse, BP - also orthostatic, SpO2).
Ask about cause (situation, medications, heart disease?).
Inform doctor (especially for first occurrence, injury, cardiac suspicion).
Check blood sugar.
Mobilize slowly, fall prevention.

verhaltensnotfall.title: Aggression
steps: Ensure self-protection! Stay calm, keep distance, secure escape route.
De-escalate situation (calm language, I-messages, validate).
No discussions, no provocation.
Get help (colleagues, security service).
Look for possible triggers (pain, fear, delirium, medications?).
Inform doctor (pharmacological sedation as ordered?).
Restraint only as last resort in acute danger after medical order!
Documentation (triggers, behavior, measures).

lungenembolie_verdacht.title: Suspected Pulmonary Embolism
steps: Recognize signs: sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia (>100/min), tachypnea, cough, anxiety, cyanosis?
Reassure patient, elevate upper body.
Inform doctor IMMEDIATELY, report suspicion!
Oxygen administration as ordered (high-flow).
Monitor vital signs closely (RR, pulse, BP, SpO2).
Prepare diagnostics (ECG, ABG, D-dimers, CT).
Prepare/give anticoagulation as ordered.
Be ready for resuscitation.

standard-dekubitus.title: Pressure Ulcer Prevention
standard-dekubitus.goal: Prevention of pressure ulcer development in at-risk individuals through early risk identification and targeted preventive measures.
structure_criteria: Nursing professionals have current knowledge about pressure ulcer development, risk factors, prevention strategies and the use of risk scales.
Appropriate pressure relief aids (e.g. special mattresses, positioning aids) are available and ready for use.
Interdisciplinary cooperation (e.g. with doctors, physiotherapists, nutritionists) is established.
process_criteria: Systematic assessment of individual pressure ulcer risk at admission and regularly or when condition changes (e.g. using Braden Scale).
Regular skin inspection, especially at predilection sites.
Promotion of patient/resident self-movement.
Regular implementation of pressure-relieving measures (position changes, micro-positioning, relief of at-risk areas).
Use of appropriate pressure-reducing aids according to risk assessment.
Ensuring adequate skin care (gentle cleansing, skin protection).
Management of nutritional and fluid deficits.
Information, education and counseling of patients/residents and their families.
Documentation of all measures and skin condition.
result_criteria: The patient's/resident's skin is intact; no pressure ulcer develops.
The patient/resident expresses satisfaction with preventive measures or experiences no unreasonable burden from them.
Early signs of skin damage are recognized and treated in time.

standard-sturz.title: Fall Prevention
standard-sturz.goal: Reduction of frequency and severity of falls through identification and minimization of individual risks and implementation of targeted prevention measures.
structure_criteria: Qualified, trained personnel for fall prevention.
Availability of appropriate aids and safe equipment (e.g. walking aids, grab bars, non-slip floors).
Systematic documentation and evaluation of fall incidents.
process_criteria: Regular, standardized risk assessment for all care recipients.
Development and implementation of individual, adapted prevention plans.
Continuous training of staff and counseling of affected individuals and their families.
result_criteria: Measurable reduction in fall rate and fall-related injuries.
Improved quality of life and sense of security for those affected.

standard-schmerz.title: Pain Management
standard-schmerz.goal: Improvement of quality of life for people with acute, chronic or expected pain through systematic pain assessment and individually adapted interventions to minimize pain experience.
structure_criteria: Qualified, trained personnel for pain assessment and management.
Availability of appropriate tools (e.g. standardized assessment instruments, training materials).
System for complete collection and evaluation of pain data.
process_criteria: Regular, comprehensive pain assessment (intensity, quality, cause, individual/cultural aspects).
Development and implementation of individual pain management plans (pharmacological and non-pharmacological).
Continuous training of staff and counseling and support of affected individuals and their families.
result_criteria: Measurable reduction in pain intensity and improvement in general well-being.
Increased satisfaction of affected individuals and their families with pain management.

standard-ernaehrung.title: Nutrition Management
standard-ernaehrung.goal: Ensuring adequate nutrition and fluid supply to prevent malnutrition and dehydration and to support healing processes and well-being.
structure_criteria: Qualified personnel with knowledge in nutrition management and screening procedures.
Availability of screening instruments (e.g. MNA, NRS) and resources for nutritional intervention (e.g. fortified diet, oral supplements, cooperation with nutritionists).
Established processes for interdisciplinary cooperation (doctors, nutritionists, speech therapists).
process_criteria: Systematic screening for malnutrition at admission and regularly.
Comprehensive assessment when at risk (eating biography, chewing/swallowing ability, BMI, needs/preferences).
Individual intervention planning (e.g. adapted diet, fortification, oral supplements, assistance with eating/drinking).
Ensuring adequate fluid intake.
Regular monitoring of food/fluid intake and weight progression.
Counseling and education of patients/residents and families.
result_criteria: The nutritional status of the patient/resident is stable or improving.
Adequate food and fluid intake is ensured.
Patients/residents express satisfaction with the nutritional situation.

mobilisation.title: Mobility Promotion
mobilisation.goal: Maintaining and promoting mobility to prevent immobility complications (e.g. contractures, thrombosis, pneumonia, pressure ulcers) and to increase independence and quality of life.
structure_criteria: Qualified personnel with knowledge of mobilization techniques and immobility risks.
Availability of appropriate aids (e.g. walking aids, transfer aids, lifts).
Cooperation with physiotherapy and occupational therapy if applicable.
process_criteria: Regular assessment of mobility status, resources and risks.
Individual planning of mobilization measures (active, assisted, passive).
Early mobilization according to medical order (especially postoperative).
Application of safe transfer and positioning techniques (e.g. according to kinesthetics).
Instruction and motivation of patient/resident for self-movement.
Integration of movement into daily activities.
Adequate pain management as prerequisite.
result_criteria: The patient/resident maintains or improves mobility within their capabilities.
Complications from immobility are prevented.
The patient/resident feels safe during mobilization measures.

entlassungsmanagement.title: Discharge Management in Nursing
entlassungsmanagement.goal: Ensuring continuous and needs-based care for patients/residents during transition from hospital or other facility to outpatient care or another form of care.
structure_criteria: Designation of a responsible nurse for discharge management.
Established cooperation and communication structures with internal and external partners (doctors, social services, therapists, follow-up care providers).
Availability of information materials for patients/families.
process_criteria: Early identification of patients/residents with post-hospital care and support needs.
Systematic assessment of individual needs (nursing, social, therapeutic).
Joint discharge planning with patient/families (setting goals, measures, organization).
Timely organization of necessary follow-up care (e.g. outpatient nursing service, aids, rehabilitation).
Ensuring information transfer (e.g. via discharge letter, nursing transfer form).
Training and counseling of patient/families for self-management.
result_criteria: The patient/resident and their families feel well prepared for discharge.
Continuity of care is ensured, care gaps are avoided.
Rehospitalizations due to care problems are reduced.

harnkontinenz.title: Promoting Urinary Continence in Nursing
harnkontinenz.goal: Maintaining or promoting urinary continence or managing incontinence to improve quality of life, prevent complications and strengthen autonomy.
structure_criteria: Qualified personnel with knowledge of continence promotion and incontinence care.
Availability of assessment instruments (e.g. voiding diary, continence profile).
Access to appropriate incontinence aids and resources for continence training.
process_criteria: Systematic assessment at admission and as needed (continence status, causes, resources, effects).
Creation of an individual continence profile.
Planning and implementation of individually adapted measures (e.g. toilet training, pelvic floor training, fluid management, aid consultation/provision, skin protection).
Counseling and instruction of patients/residents and families.
Regular evaluation of measures and adaptation of plan.
result_criteria: The patient/resident achieves optimal continence or adequate compensation for incontinence.
Skin complications related to incontinence are prevented.
The quality of life and social participation of the patient/resident improve.

chronische_wunden.title: Care of People with Chronic Wounds
chronische_wunden.goal: Promoting wound healing, preventing wound infections, reducing pain and odor, and improving quality of life in people with chronic wounds (e.g. pressure ulcers, venous leg ulcers, diabetic foot syndrome).
structure_criteria: Qualified personnel with specific knowledge in wound management (e.g. wound experts ICW/DGfW).
Availability of appropriate materials for wound diagnostics and therapy (modern wound dressings, bandage materials).
Established interdisciplinary cooperation (doctors of various specialties, podiatrists, etc.).
process_criteria: Comprehensive assessment: evaluation of wound (location, size, depth, wound base, exudate, odor, pain) and patient (underlying diseases, nutritional status, mobility, psychosocial factors).
Planning and implementation of phase-appropriate local wound therapy (debridement, wound cleansing, exudate management, selection of appropriate dressings).
Management of wound-related symptoms (pain, odor, itching).
Support of causal therapy (e.g. compression therapy for venous leg ulcers, pressure relief for pressure ulcers).
Measures for recurrence prevention.
Counseling, instruction and training of patient/families for self-management.
Regular evaluation and adaptation of therapy plan.
result_criteria: Wound healing progresses, wound size reduces.
Signs of infection are prevented or treated early.
Wound-related pain and other symptoms are alleviated.
The patient's quality of life and self-care ability improve.

geburt.title: Promoting Physiological Birth
geburt.goal: Supporting and promoting natural birth process while considering the physical and psychological needs of the woman, to minimize interventions and enable a positive birth experience.
structure_criteria: Midwife-led care is available and supported.
Appropriate spatial and material conditions for physiological births (e.g. birthing pool, alternative birthing positions).
Clear communication pathways and cooperation in the interprofessional team (midwives, doctors, anesthesia).
process_criteria: Continuous 1:1 care by a midwife during the active birth phase.
Promotion of mobility and free choice of birth position by the woman.
Use of non-pharmacological methods for pain relief (e.g. water birth, massage, breathing).
Restrained use of interventions (e.g. labor-enhancing medications, episiotomy) according to indication.
Respectful communication and shared decision-making with the woman.
Immediate and undisturbed skin-to-skin contact between mother and child after birth (bonding).
result_criteria: The rate of spontaneous vaginal births is high.
The rate of medical interventions is low.
Women report a positive birth experience and high satisfaction with care.
Maternal and neonatal morbidity related to birth is low.

CareBuddy serves as a support and reference tool for medical professionals. It does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. In case of emergency, please contact a doctor or emergency services (112).

The provided content, particularly regarding diseases, emergency measures and ICD-10 codes, has been carefully compiled but makes no claim to completeness or freedom from errors. Use of the app is at your own responsibility.

For medical decisions, always consult official guidelines and current professional literature.

privacy_ai_text:
The app uses an AI function for the Care Buddy AI Chat. When using the AI chat, your chat requests are transmitted for processing to a server by Mark Tietz (Königplatz 3, 87448 Waltenhofen). Your questions and the corresponding AI responses are stored on this server to answer future requests faster and improve performance.

The following data is processed:
• Your chat requests: The texts you enter are transmitted to the above-mentioned server.
• Server-side question-answer history: To improve response times and performance, your questions and the AI-generated responses are stored on Mark Tietz's server.

No chat content is stored locally on your device (except for temporary display in the chat window during use). We expressly point out that the questions and answers stored on the server may be used to improve the AI. Therefore, do not share sensitive personal data (such as patient information) in the chat. The chat function is designed as a general information source and is not intended for discussing individual cases.
privacy_security_text: We use appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure the security of your data. Since app data is only stored locally on your device, we recommend protecting your device with a password/PIN and creating regular backups.
privacy_changes_text: This privacy policy may be updated occasionally. Changes will be published with an app update. We recommend reviewing this privacy policy regularly.

disclaimer_important_note: This app does not replace professional advice, diagnosis or treatment by licensed doctors or medical professionals. For health questions or complaints, always consult a qualified professional. In case of emergency, call the emergency services (112).
disclaimer_liability_1: The contents of the CareBuddy app are created with the greatest possible care and regularly updated. Nevertheless, CareBuddy assumes no liability for the accuracy, completeness or timeliness of the information provided. Use is at your own risk. Use of the app does not create a legally binding contractual relationship between the user and the provider.
disclaimer_liability_2: All content in the app serves exclusively for information and education in the nursing context. CareBuddy does not make diagnoses, give medical recommendations and does not replace medical or therapeutic advice. The use of the content - especially calculators, recommendations or general information - is at your own responsibility and must be checked for accuracy and appropriateness before use. The app is intended exclusively for trained professionals.
disclaimer_liability_3: Where care standards, dosages or scores are given, these serve only for general orientation. They do not replace individual assessment in individual cases. Information on laws, guidelines or standards may be outdated or incomplete - it is recommended to always consult official sources.
disclaimer_liability_4: The integrated calculators, scores and tools are based on known professional sources and have been carefully implemented. Nevertheless, no liability can be assumed for their results. They serve exclusively educational purposes and not for direct application to patients.
disclaimer_liability_5: CareBuddy is designed as a supplementary digital tool, not as a replacement for sound professional knowledge, practical experience or institutional training.
disclaimer_ai_1: The Care Buddy AI Chat uses artificial intelligence (AI) to generate responses. AI-generated content may be inaccurate, misleading or outdated. The AI can make mistakes and is not a source of binding medical or nursing information. All responses provided by the AI should be critically reviewed and compared with current professional information.
disclaimer_ai_2: The AI is not intended for diagnostic purposes, therapy decisions or as a replacement for professional medical advice. Use the AI only as a supplementary information tool and never as the sole basis for decisions in patient care.
disclaimer_emergency: The emergency measures described in the app do not replace training in first aid or medical emergency care. In case of emergency, immediately call the emergency services (112) and/or consult medical professionals.
disclaimer_links: If CareBuddy links to or embeds external content (e.g. Wikipedia, ICD-10, manufacturer information), we assume no responsibility for their content. The operators of external sites are exclusively responsible for the content of external sites.
disclaimer_copyright: All content published within the app is subject to German copyright law. Reproduction, distribution or other use outside the narrow limits of copyright is not permitted without prior written consent. The display of CareBuddy content in external frames or applications is only permitted with express permission.
disclaimer_privacy: By using this app, you accept our privacy policy. More information can be found in the privacy policy in the settings.

tips: Proper hand disinfection takes at least 30 seconds.
Normal blood pressure is about 120/80 mmHg.
If you suspect a stroke, think FAST: Face, Arms, Speech, Time.
Oxygen saturation should normally be above 95%.
For chest compressions: 100-120 compressions per minute.
Normal body temperature is between 36.5°C and 37.4°C.
Fall prevention is one of the most important measures in nursing.
Documentation should always be done promptly after nursing care.
In case of shortness of breath, sit the patient up and calm them.
Hypoglycemia often manifests as restlessness, sweating and trembling.
In case of suspected stroke, every minute counts – call 112, don't waste time!
In case of suspected allergy or anaphylaxis: keep emergency kit ready immediately.
Fever is measurable from 38.0°C – from 38.5°C it is considered high fever.
After a fall, always watch for pain, bruising and neurological signs.
Dehydration often shows through dry lips and standing skin folds.
Suddenly occurring chest pain can be an emergency – act immediately!
A seizure under 5 minutes is usually harmless – still observe carefully.
For bleeding, always apply direct pressure and cover wound as sterile as possible.
Hand disinfection is one of the most important measures for infection prevention.
When administering medication, always follow the 5-R principle: Right patient, right medication, right dose, right time, right route.
Regular mobilization prevents thrombosis and pneumonia.
Good communication with patients and relatives is an important component of care.
Fluid intake and output should be monitored regularly in at-risk patients.
Fall prevention begins at admission – recognize and document risk factors.
Pressure ulcers are preventable – regular positioning and skin inspection are essential.
Always ask about pain and adjust pain therapy individually.
Emergency medications should always be readily available and regularly checked for expiration dates.
Documentation should be timely and factual – it is also legally important.
